question: Why did we choose FastAPI for this project?
answer: We chose FastAPI for its automatic OpenAPI docs, async support, and Pydantic-based validation. Key dependencies: uvicorn, httpx, psutil, pyside6, pyautogui.

question: Why use FastAPI with Python?
answer: We chose FastAPI for its automatic OpenAPI docs, async support, and Pydantic-based validation. Key dependencies: uvicorn, httpx, psutil, pyside6, pyautogui.

question: How should duplicate condition adjectives or nouns be handled in descriptions?
answer: Group them using a / separator without spaces. Prioritize common prefixes (adjectives) followed by common suffixes (nouns). Recognized separators: ' to ', ' through ', ' on '.

question: Should flaws be grouped if they share a noun but have different prepositions/separators?
answer: Yes. If separators differ (e.g., 'to' vs 'through'), the full 'prefix + separator' part is grouped (e.g., 'cut-mark to/drill-hole through Artwork').

question: Why: Initial commit: Production ready version?
answer: (Auto-drafted from commit 2ce331f on 2026-05-11.) Please review and expand with actual reasoning.

question: Why did we add the 'Send Page to WYSIWYG Scraper' context menu item?
answer: To allow scraping the currently active Discogs release or master page by right-clicking on the page background, while preserving the existing right-click scraper behavior for links.

question: Why did we strip the '--- Scraped via Master Release ---' header line in html_format.py?
answer: To prevent it from being processed as the album header in the generated HTML description on the Details tab, while still keeping the label in the raw text/history.

question: Why did we rename the CD Matrix, Tape, and LP crop mode radio buttons to Custom1, Custom2, and Custom3 in WysiScan?
answer: To generalize the crop mode labels in the scanner UI for the user, while preserving all underlying code, API endpoints, and processing logic (which still reference 'cd', 'tape', and 'lp' values).

question: Why did we move and rename the Full, Open Image, and Save This Image buttons in WysiScan?
answer: To group cropped image action buttons together at the bottom of the section in an equally spaced flex row, simplifying their labels to 'Full', 'Open', and 'Save' to maintain clean spacing and visual clarity.

question: Why did we replace WysiScan's image placeholders with a custom SVG saying 'Scan or Import now'?
answer: To improve UX by showing a clear call-to-action ('Scan or Import now') when no image is loaded (and after group resets), while also resolving a corrupted inline SVG on the cropped image preview.

question: Why did we rename the Help button in WysiScan to Hot Keys?
answer: To more accurately reflect that the button launches a list of hotkeys and keyboard shortcuts, improving the clarity of the header UI controls.

question: Why did we remove the Tips section from the Hot Keys modal in WysiScan?
answer: To focus the modal purely on keyboard shortcuts now that the button has been renamed to 'Hot Keys', decluttering the help UI.

question: Why did we move WysiScan's Clear button to the input group next to Start Group?
answer: To group the Group Name action controls ('Start Group' and 'Clear') together on the same horizontal line, styling both buttons consistently in height, padding, and layout alignment.

question: Why did we disable the Scan, Import, and Crop buttons in WysiScan when the Group Name is manually typed?
answer: To prevent accidental scan/import/crop actions into a group that has not been initialized or resumed, forcing the user to commit the group name by hitting 'Start Group' or pressing Enter.

question: Why did we relocate WysiScan's refresh button to Group Actions and rename 'Scan Group' to 'Group'?
answer: To group all group-level controls ('Refresh', 'Save Marked', 'Delete Marked', 'Open Folder') together in the top sidebar panel, and to shorten the main gallery section header to 'Group'.

question: Why did we replace WysiScan's sidebar button text labels with icons (💾, 🗑️, 📂)?
answer: To streamline and compact the Group Actions toolbar layout in the sidebar, replacing long text buttons with standard visual emojis and hover titles.

question: Why did we implement group and individual file renaming in WysiScan?
answer: To allow renaming either a single selected file (fully customizable filename) or an entire group of selected files (keeping their numeric suffixes _1, _2 intact) using a dedicated modal popup, while maintaining related temp, backup, and redo files in sync.

question: Why did we update the rename file/group logic to handle identical paths and auto-sync single file group renames?
answer: To prevent FileExistsError exceptions on Windows when a file is renamed to its current name, and to automatically detect when a single file is renamed to a pattern with a numeric suffix (e.g. Vlad_6) and update the active gallery group prefix to keep it visible.

question: Why did we replace the WysiScan gallery checkbox headers with the actual file names?
answer: To make it easier for the user to see the exact filenames of their scans and renamed files directly in the gallery list, while removing redundant labels at the bottom.

question: Why did we move the WysiScan gallery checkboxes to the left of the filenames?
answer: To match the standard UI pattern of placing selection checkboxes before the items they control, improving scan selection scanning.

question: Why did we configure the manual crop modal to open without a default selection box?
answer: To provide a clean canvas for manual cropping by disabling auto-cropping and bounds detection inside the crop modal, making it easier for the user to draw their own crop box immediately.

question: Why did we make the WysiScan gallery thumbnails smaller, move the Select All checkbox next to Group Actions (removing the Group header), and move the EXIT button to the top header?
answer: To optimize sidebar space, align selection controls with actions, and clean up the toolbar by moving administrative exit actions to the top navigation header next to theme/keys.

question: Why did we add CloseApplications=force and optimize process termination in the Inno Setup installer?
answer: To prevent installation updates from failing due to locked files (like WYSIWYG.exe). We resolved this by: 1) enabling CloseApplications=force to leverage Windows Restart Manager, 2) using ExpandConstant('{sys}\taskkill.exe') to avoid issues with broken PATH variables, and 3) adding a Sleep(1500) delay to let the OS fully release file handles after processes exit.

question: Why did we add an 'Open' button next to the LP / CD / CASS. CONDITION multiselects, and what should it do?
answer: The multiselects only show ~4 rows at a time and display only option titles, so users could not see all options or their full description text. The new 'Open' button (stacked below 'Clear', all three buttons shortened to an identical 70x18px to fit beside the 65px-tall selects) opens a 'Select Conditions' modal listing every option with its full text in three columns; clicking a row toggles the matching multiselect selection live (no apply step needed). The modal is draggable by its header, resizable, and its lists redraw/fill on resize per docs/CONVENTIONS.md. Options were considered and rejected: previewing selected text in a popup, duplicating the Edit modal, and loading the master Conditions.json from the FYRShare server.

question: Why do selected rows in the Select Conditions modal use black text, and why does the modal reset its size/position on every open?
answer: Dark mode forces white text inside modals (styles.css .modal-content color: #fff), but selected rows keep the light-blue highlight (--wysiwyg-blue-light #e6f0ff, undefined in dark mode), so white-on-light-blue was unreadable. Selected rows now force color #000 (title) and #444 (description) in both themes; unselected rows keep the theme text color. The modal also resets its inline style (position/margin/left/top/width/height) to the captured default on every open, because a user dragged it off-screen and could no longer reach the drag header to move it back.

question: Why does the tiny Open button next to the PACKAGING FEATURE label read options from the select itself instead of a shared data source, and why was the modal drag logic refactored?
answer: The packaging picker renders rows straight from #packagingFeature's own <option> elements (skipping the empty-value '-- None --' placeholder) so the modal always matches whatever initializeDropdowns loaded from /settings, with no second data source to drift. The draggable/resizable/reset-on-open behavior previously lived in a condition-picker-specific IIFE; it was extracted into a shared initDraggableModal(contentId, headerId) that returns a reset function, applied to both the Select Conditions and Select Packaging Feature modals, so the two cannot drift apart.

question: Why do EDITION, FORMAT TAGS, WEIGHT/SPEED, PRE FM, POST FM and SLEEVE PACKAGING share one list-picker modal instead of getting one modal each?
answer: All six (plus packaging feature) are multiple-selects populated identically by populateDropdown from /settings data, so their pickers behave identically. One config-driven modal (LIST_PICKER_CONFIGS: selectId + label + title) keyed off each tiny button's data-picker attribute avoids seven duplicate modals/render functions and keeps them from drifting. Rows are read live from each select's own <option> elements (skipping the '-- None --' placeholder), so the modal always reflects whatever /settings loaded. The seven tiny buttons share the .list-picker-open-btn utility class in styles.css for pixel parity.

question: How does the Select Conditions modal search bar filter options, and what are the edge-case rules?
answer: A single search input above the three columns filters every column live on each 'input' event: case-insensitive substring match against each option's title + text concatenated; an empty (or whitespace-only) query shows all options. Columns with zero matches show a 'No matches' message (distinct from 'No options' when the category itself has no data). Filtering is view-only — it never clears selections, toggles work on filtered rows, and the field is reset to empty whenever the modal is opened. The same search was NOT added to the shared list-picker modal (edition/format tags/etc.) because it was not requested.

question: How does the HTML tab LIVE PREVIEW editing work, and which direction does the sync go?
answer: LIVE PREVIEW is now a contenteditable div; every 'input' event serializes its DOM into the HTML CODE textarea (preview -> code only, per request). Formatting uses document.execCommand with styleWithCSS forced false so output is <b>/<u>/<i> tags (eBay-description friendly) rather than inline CSS. Toolbar buttons use mousedown preventDefault so the preview selection survives the click, and a selectionchange listener toggles their active state from queryCommandState, which also clears when the selection leaves the preview. Ctrl+B/U/I work natively inside the editable. The Generate HTML Description flow still overwrites both boxes, so code edits made by hand in the textarea are not pushed back into the preview (not requested).

question: Why is the Adds > Discogs menu item hidden instead of deleted?
answer: The Discogs Adds feature does not work and is not a priority, so the item is hidden with an inline display:none rather than removed. The button and its openAddsDiscogs click wiring (addClickListener null-checks safely) are kept intact so the item can be restored by dropping the inline style if the feature is ever fixed. The Adds submenu still shows Amazon.

question: Should the assistant test changes itself?
answer: No. The user tests every change themselves and reports problems back. Do not spin up servers, drive browsers, run test harnesses, or otherwise verify UI/behavior after making an edit — make the change, log it, and hand it over. Cheap syntax checks (node --check) are still acceptable. Recorded in AGENTS.md under Project Instructions.

question: Why did the Amazon Adds View (Full/Small) and Jump-to-Section dropdowns stop working, and how are they wired now?
answer: Both used inline onchange attributes (onAapViewChange / onAapSectionNav) but the page's script is an async IIFE, so those functions were not globals and the handlers threw ReferenceError. Fix: removed the inline onchange attributes and wired 'change' listeners inside the IIFE next to the page's existing button wiring, keeping the functions private. The View dropdown re-renders the cached lastText (no re-scrape); the Section dropdown scrolls to the section title and resets itself so the same entry can be re-picked.

question: Why do the Amazon Adds topbar dropdowns force black text on a white background in dark mode instead of using the theme text color?
answer: The View (Full/Small) and Jump to Section selects used color: var(--text), which is light (#e6e6e6) in dark mode and was unreadable on the native dropdown surfaces. Scoped to body.dark, both selects now force color #000 with a white background so the closed control and the open popup stay readable, matching native select appearance rather than the dark panel.

question: Why do Amazon Adds Brand Name / Manufacturer truncate at a spaced dash instead of the first hyphen?
answer: Both fields were carrying extra text after the label name (catalog/press info). They now keep only the part before the first dash that has whitespace on its left side (hyphen, en-dash or em-dash), so 'Atlantic - 1978 pressing' becomes 'Atlantic'. Unspaced hyphens are deliberately preserved because catalog numbers (314-526) and real label names (Anti-, Zoth-Ommog) contain them. Applied only to the two output fields inside generate_final_amazon_table; Label_List, Html_Label_Display, keyword blocking and the self-release/check-box fallback logic are unchanged. An all-dash or empty result falls back to the original value.

question: Why does /api/changelog sort entries instead of slicing the file?
answer: The app-title click opens Version History from GET /api/changelog. It used to take entries[-3:] reversed, which assumed the changelog is append-ordered, but changelog.txt is maintained newest-first (newest section at the top) and also contains legacy entries appended at the bottom (v1.8-v1.9 from May 2026), so the modal always showed ancient entries. The endpoint now parses each entry header for a date (YYYY-MM-DD) and version tuple, sorts descending, and returns the newest three, which is correct for both newest-first and append-order files. Only the top 3 are shown, unchanged from before. PITFALL: the version regex's 4th group is optional, so vm.groups() contains None for 3-part headers (v1.2.1) — convert with int(p) if p else 0, otherwise int(None) throws and the endpoint's bare except returns zero entries (blank Version History).

question: What was bumped for the 1.14.0.0 release and why do all four version fields matter?
answer: version.json moved from 1.13.5.8 to 1.14.0.0 with last_updated 2026-10-12, and major/minor/patch/build were all set (1/14/0/0) because /api/version compares the local tuple against the server version.json tuple to decide whether an update is available. Today's changelog entries were moved under a new '### v1.14.0.0 - 2026-10-12' header at the top of changelog.txt (newest-first), leaving the pre-existing v1.13.5.8 WysiScan entries under their original header.

question: How does the Amazon Adds Genre/Style Copy button strip commas, and why only that row?
answer: The per-row Copy handler in Adds/amazon_add_page.html checks the row textarea's data-label (set at render time from the 'Label - Value' line); for Genre/Style it copies value.replace(/\s*,\s*/g, ' ').trim(), collapsing 'Latin, Mariachi' to 'Latin Mariachi' so the clipboard text has single spaces, not the double space a literal comma->space swap would leave. The visible textarea keeps the commas and Copy All is unchanged (not requested). The clipboard-API fallback path (select + execCommand) still copies the raw textarea text in that edge case. The field label itself is already 'Genre/Style' in Adds/Amazon_add_scraper.py (previously Genre_Style) - it only appears after an app restart because the module is imported at startup.

question: Where does the Amazon Adds 'Add New' button live and how does it add keyword lines?
answer: It sits beside the Copy All button in the Subject Keyword group's own action row (kw-actions, not the top toolbar's Copy All), because that is the Copy All attached to the keyword list. Row construction was extracted into buildKeywordLine(tok) and is now shared by the scraper render path and the Add New click handler, which appends buildKeywordLine('') to the group's .kw-list and focuses the new textarea. The new line is picked up automatically by the group's Copy All and the top Copy All (both read live DOM values; empty lines are skipped when joining). Lines added this way are lost on a Full/Small re-render, same as manual keyword edits, because renderResults rebuilds from the last scraped text - pre-existing behavior, not changed here. BUG FOUND AFTER FIRST IMPLEMENTATION: the button initially had class 'kw-copyline kw-addnew' (to reuse the styling), so the earlier closest('.kw-copyline') branch in the shared results click handler captured the click and ran the keyword copy instead, making Add New look dead. Fixed by giving the button its own class only and sharing the base styles via a grouped '.kw-copyline, .kw-addnew' CSS rule - never share a class between a styled element and an existing delegated-handler branch selector.

question: Why did Country/Region of Origin always come out United States, and what is the new behavior?
answer: generate_discogs_data hardcoded final_origin = 'United States' with a comment claiming it was the selling origin, ignoring the Discogs Country: line it had already parsed into raw_country_line. Per user request the field now reports the release's actual Discogs country (Canada for the Branikald example), normalized through the existing country_map (US/USA/Worldwide -> United States, UK/UK & Europe -> United Kingdom, Europe -> Germany, Australasia -> Australia), case-insensitively; unmapped values pass through unchanged, and missing/none/unknown/n/a falls back to United States. KNOWN SIDE EFFECT (kept intentionally): is_import = final_origin not in ['United States'] now evaluates True for non-US releases, so they regain the Import format tag that the hardcoded value had silently suppressed. Flagged to the user in case the Import tag is unwanted.

question: Why did the hamburger Edit Counters option open nothing, and what does the editor now do?
answer: openCounterEditor() built its buttons array with onClick: closeModal, but closeModal was never defined anywhere (git log -S shows it has only ever been referenced, since the counter system commit), so a ReferenceError was thrown before showModal() ran and no modal appeared. Added closeModal() (hides #genericModal) next to showModal(); this also fixes the Reports modal, which referenced the same missing function. Per the user's spec the editor keeps 4 default counters and allows adding up to 2 more (MAX_COUNTERS 7 -> 6), and each row edits the button's background color and label text plus reorder (up/down) and delete. UX fix: Add Counter / move / delete now call commitCounterEditorInputs() first, because re-rendering the modal used to discard typed label/color edits that had not been saved yet.

question: What is the counters' 'FILE TEXT', why is it editable, and what happens when it is renamed?
answer: FILE TEXT is the counter's serverKey: incrementCounter POSTs {type, label} = serverKey, and main.py's /api/increment-counter writes '{label}: {count}' lines into the daily counts file (get_today_counts_data), so that string IS the text behind the button. The Edit Counters modal now shows a labeled FILE TEXT input per row (previously hidden/uneditable, auto 'New N' for added counters) and Save persists it; a cleared value keeps the previous key so a button can never silently increment nothing. Adding a counter starts from editable placeholders (label NEW, file text New N) and focuses the new row's FILE TEXT input. CAVEAT surfaced to the user: renaming an existing counter re-points the button at the new tally line and the old 'OldKey: n' line simply stops being read/updated (both lines can coexist in the day's file). Row values are HTML-escaped when rendered into the modal.

question: Does the WysiScan Image Convert source-folder scan recurse into subfolders?
answer: No - it is already root-only. WysiScan/imageconvert/app.py _scan_for_images uses os.listdir(folder_path) plus an os.path.isfile() check, so only files directly in the selected folder are converted and subfolders (e.g. C:\New Scans\8163\a) are skipped. This is the only scan in the conversion flow (both the WysiScan page's /batch-convert -> app.py --source CLI path and the standalone GUI's select_folder_dialog use it); scanner_server.py, scanner_test.html and the imageconvert JS contain no os.walk/rglob/glob/recursive scan. Committed long ago as ad02cab 'convert root-only images'. On 2026-10-12 the user reported recursion because their working copy predated that commit until ~16:22 that day; no code change was needed, just a retry (WysiScan runs from source there and spawns app.py fresh per conversion, so no restart required). Do not re-fix this.

question: Why does the MEDIA DESCRIPTION multiselect share Conditions.json and both condition modals?
answer: The user asked for a multiselect beside MEDIA DESCRIPTION backed by the same Conditions.json. Rather than a separate data store, 'media' became a fourth key in customOptionsData (alongside lp/cd/cassette): /api/conditions and /api/save-conditions already read/write the whole object, so edits flow to the same file with no endpoint changes. It renders into a new #mediaOptions multiselect (110px, 65px tall, 11px font, beside a horizontally shrunk MEDIA DESCRIPTION input inside the same form-group cell so no other GUI elements move), is edited through the Edit Conditions modal's new 'Media Description' category, and is selectable through the Select Conditions picker as a fourth MEDIA DESCRIPTION column (search, click-to-toggle, Clear All included). Selecting an option writes its text into the MEDIA DESCRIPTION input space-joined (syncMediaOptionsToTextBox on change and on picker toggle), so generation consumes it exactly like typed text. Right-click favoriting, parsePastedData and Reset All cover the new select generically. Note: Clear/Clear All clear the multiselect selections but intentionally leave the text box alone so manually typed descriptions are never destroyed. Conditions.json was seeded with 5 starter media entries.

question: Why did right-click Favorite/Unfavorite do nothing on the Media Condition multiselect?
answer: Bug in app.js favoriteContextItem.onclick select-element branch: for targetId 'mediaConditionOptions' it resolved the data key as currentConditionMediaType (lp/cd/cassette), but media condition items live in the separate customOptionsData.mediaCondition array, so the title/text find never matched and nothing toggled. Fixed by keying 'mediaConditionOptions' to customOptionsData.mediaCondition and matching on title + text + media_type (media_type check is skipped for legacy lp/cd/cassette options). Modal-row favoriting already used customOptionsData.mediaCondition and was unaffected; Sleeve Condition and legacy multiselects unchanged. renderCustomOptionsSelect() re-renders the condition multiselects via renderConditionMultiselects() so the star updates, and saveCustomOptions() persists the whole object including the toggled favorite flag.

question: Why does the WysiScan Extract Text OPEN button output only the clean extracted text?
answer: User reported the OPEN button in the Extract Text From Image(s) modal (WysiScan/scanner_test.html, served by scanner_server.py) was not opening correctly - it dumped 'Selected Images', the Prompt, an 'Extracted Text:' header, and the result box innerText which included Copy/Copy Desc. button labels and CSS-uppercased section headers. Fixed on the client only (server /open-in-notepad in scanner_server.py already writes the text and os.startfile's it). renderCliResults now stores the raw output in lastCliResultText and tags rendered elements with data attributes: data-cli-header on section headers, data-cli-label on entry rows (label text, empty string when no label), data-cli-media on the Media Description block. New buildCliPlainText() walks #cliResultBox direct children and rebuilds plain text: 'Label: value' entry rows, 'Section:' headers, and the Media Description textarea verbatim, honoring user edits to the textareas; falls back to lastCliResultText when the DOM yields nothing. openCliInNotepad() now sends only that text (toast warn if empty). lastCliResultText resets when the modal is opened. Do NOT re-add the selected-images/prompt headers - user wants only Label/Text, Tracks, Extras, and Media Description in Notepad.

question: Why does the WysiScan Extract Text Notepad output use group labels, blank lines between groups, and a Media Description header?
answer: Follow-up to the OPEN-button fix: user wanted the Notepad dump formatted with 'Release:', 'Tracks:', 'Extra:' group labels, a blank line between groups, and a 'Media Description:' group label above the shell/matrix data (their reference layout shows groups separated by an empty line, entries as 'Label: value', tracks as 'A1: Title'). buildCliPlainText in WysiScan/scanner_test.html now inserts a blank line before every group header and before the Media Description block (never before the first line), and the media block pushes its own header taken from data-cli-mediaHeader (set from the rendered 'Media Description' head in flushMedia, colon appended if missing) above the textarea contents. Entry rows and section headers are otherwise unchanged; entries and the media textarea value stay verbatim (user edits in the textareas are reflected). Multiple consecutive blank lines are collapsed and the whole output is trimmed.

question: Why does the media/sleeve flaw region have exactly one 'with ' clause?
answer: User reported casette example 'Used Like New 1993 USA Cassette with shelf-wear/scuffing with holes in the Shell & missing ink / scuff marks / stained Shell / wrinkled tape is Out-of-Print with 15 Tracks - ...' had TWO 'with ' statements when the MEDIA DESCRIPTION text box is empty and many MEDIA CONDITION multiselect items are selected. Root cause: the Sleeve Condition fallback (else { finalFormatString += ' with ' + combinedFlaws; } in processFormatData) fires exactly when there is no text box text, appending ' with shelf-wear/scuffing' (Conditions.json cassette 'Shelf Wear' text) to finalFormatString, while the new mediaconditionPhrase added its own 'with ' on top. Fix on the media side only (Sleeve logic untouched, per the user's earlier constraint): mediaconditionPhrase adds 'with ' only when BOTH the phrase does not already start with 'with ' AND /\swith\s\S/i does not match finalFormatString (i.e. no preceding with-clause already introduces the list). NOTE: the prior-with regex is whitespace + literal with + whitespace + non-whitespace (case-insensitive); an earlier attempt wrote an extra leading space inside the literal (space + space-with-space), which never matches and silently reintroduced the double with-clause. Verified region counts (finalFormatString + phrase only, excluding the unrelated later 'with N Tracks' clause): shelf+media no textbox -> 1; media only -> 1; textbox+media -> 1; textbox only -> 1; textbox or item already starting with 'with ' -> 1; Final Sale + textbox -> 1 (Final Sale stays bare, ahead of the phrase).

question: Why do media description/media-condition flaws always precede sleeve flaws?
answer: User example: with no text box text, MEDIA CONDITION 'Missing Ink' (text 'missing ink') plus SLEEVE multiselect 'Cellophane Tearing' + 'Cracking (Jewel Case)' produced 'Cassette with Cellophane tearing & Jewel Case cracking missing ink' (sleeve flaws before media flaw). Root cause: the sleeve custom-options block ran first and, in its fallback path (no sleeveCond/sleeveDesc/sleevePkg/postFM/text box text), appended sleeve flaws onto finalFormatString, which precedes mediaconditionPhrase in assembleDescription. Restructured processFormatData into 4 ordered steps: (1) collect media entries - text box text first, then media multiselect flaws, Final Sale (media) into mediaFinalSale, clear mediaDesc; (2) collect sleeve entries, Final Sale (sleeve) appended bare to finalFormatString as the exception to the media-first rule; (3) place sleeve entries keeping Case A (sleeveCond+sleeveDesc), Case B (conditionPhrase after sleevePkg), the sleevePkg path and the hasSleeveDesc path untouched, but replacing the postFM/mediaDesc/else fallbacks with: when hasMediaContent, concat grouped sleeve entries AFTER the media entries so they flow through mediaconditionPhrase, otherwise keep the old ' with ' + combined on finalFormatString; (4) build mediaconditionPhrase from mediaEntries with the single-with guard. Result for the user case: 'Cassette with missing ink & Cellophane tearing / Jewel Case cracking'; exception case keeps Final Sale leading: 'Cassette ( final sale - ... ) with missing ink & Cellophane tearing'; sleeve-only output unchanged; postFM-only output unchanged. NOTE the old 'else if (mediaDesc)' sleeve path was absorbed: the text box text is a media entry so it still leads, which also fixes sleeve flaws previously landing between text box text and media multiselect flaws.

question: Why does the Select Conditions search bar filter the currently open list instead of switching to Media?
answer: Bug: open Sleeve (Current Type) then type in the search bar switched the list to Media, because the search input handler always re-rendered via renderConditionPicker() which defaults to Media Condition in single-column mode. Fix: a module-level conditionPickerRedraw callback that every picker-open function registers (openConditionPickerForMedia/Sleeve, openMediaCondition/SleeveConditionThreeColumnModal, openDualColumnConditionPicker, renderConditionPicker); the search handler calls it to re-filter the currently open view and only falls back to renderConditionPicker() when no view is registered. Openers accept preserveSearch: fresh opens (context menu, Open button) clear the search, in-modal re-renders (selection toggles) pass preserveSearch=true so the query survives. Empty states show No matches vs No options. Secondary fix: /app.js served with Cache-Control no-cache in main.py because heuristic browser caching of FileResponse kept serving stale app.js after edits, masking applied fixes during local use.

question: Why does .agents/rules/tokensaver.md exist and what takes precedence on token use?
answer: Project-level token-saver rules (trigger: always_on) added by the user, mirroring the global token saver instructions: token efficiency overrides all other rules; no self-verification of code (user verifies and reports issues); output only the requested file changes with no pleasantries/explanations/diffs and finish with Complete; no planning outputs unless massive refactor ordered; minimal code comments; narrow file reads to explicitly requested files unless mechanically broken without them.

question: Why hide the dual-column "Both" checkbox in Select Conditions Open Media / Open Sleeve (All Types)?
answer: In the three-column All Types layouts there is nothing to toggle: LP/CD/Cassette media conditions are already shown side by side, and the sleeve all types are columns below. Keeping the checkbox visible produced a visual mismatch when it retained its checked state from an earlier session. Fix: every picker-open function now calls setDualColumnToggle(visible, checked) - hide + uncheck for the two All Types views, show + uncheck for the current-type single views, show + check for the shared dual view. renderConditionPicker restores the box on the single-column default path (OPEN button / unchecking). The checkbox stays functional in the current-type Media/Sleeve views, where it toggles between the single list and the Media+Sleeve dual column.

question: Why does unchecking "Both" from a sleeve-opened single view return to the sleeve list instead of Media Condition?
answer: Bug: opening Sleeve (Current Type) then checking and unchecking "Both" collapsed back to Media Condition. Fix: track which single column the modal was opened from via conditionPickerSingleSource (set to "media" in openConditionPickerForMedia and renderConditionPicker, "sleeve" in openConditionPickerForSleeve). The dualColumnMode change handler restores that source on uncheck (sleeve -> openConditionPickerForSleeve, media -> renderConditionPicker), preserving the search query (preserveSearch=true) and syncing currentModalCategory to match. Fresh opens (context menu / Open button) still default to Media Condition, and Open Media (All Types) / Open Sleeve (All Types) hide the "Both" toggle entirely.

question: Why do the Select Conditions list headers always include the active media format?
answer: Bug: after checking and unchecking "Both" the single column collapsed to a generic "Media Condition" header, losing the CD/LP/CASSETTE context that the dual view had shown ("CD MEDIA CONDITION" / "CD SLEEVE CONDITION"). Fix: getConditionPickerConfigs now builds labels from currentConditionMediaType in both single and dual mode, so the column headers read "CD MEDIA CONDITION" / "CD SLEEVE CONDITION" / "LP MEDIA CONDITION" etc. The modal title header and the dedicated openConditionPickerForMedia / openConditionPickerForSleeve / openDualColumnConditionPicker openers already prefixed the media type, so the generic renderConditionPicker path was the only inconsistent one.

question: Why does the accent text color switch from blue to yellow only in Dark Mode?
answer: Blue (#0000FF) text is unreadable in Dark Mode: on the #1e1e1e panel it is only 1.9:1 contrast. But pure #FFFF00 text on the Light Mode white surfaces would be 1.07:1 and equally unreadable, and blue text on white is fine (8.6:1). So a theme-aware token was introduced instead of a blind swap: --wysiwyg-accent-text (main app) and --primary-text (WysiScan) = #0000FF in Light Mode, #FFFF00 in Dark Mode. Every place the accent was used as TEXT now uses that token: the main app's 7 modal/picker titles (index.html), the Settings Editor's dynamic category title color and its border-bottom (editor.html), WysiScan's "Image Convert" panel label and the cliStatusMsg status line in the OCR modal footer. Blue used as a BACKGROUND (h2 header bar, .scraper-button, .search-button, .hk-key-btn.capturing, .save-bar and modal-footer borders, .history-sidebar border, WysiScan h1/menu-btn/buttons) was left unchanged because it carries white or yellow text. The main app's hamburger button keeps blue text because it sits on a yellow button background (yellow-on-yellow would be invisible). This generalises the pattern the Adds pages already used (--accent #0000ff in Light Mode, #ffd400 in Dark Mode); their dark accent was aligned to the same #FFFF00 yellow, and UberPaste's dark-mode "keep" marker was changed from cyan #00FFFF to #FFFF00 for family consistency (its Light Mode #0000FF marker stays).

question: Why upgrade AnyIO to 4.14.2?
answer: Pinned AnyIO to 4.14.2 in both requirements snapshots to include the TLS IDNA certificate matching and subprocess stderr deadlock fixes; AnyIO 4.14.0 also adds TaskHandle returns, slots on core classes, and tighter typing, while 4.14.2 changes invalid ByteReceiveStream receive sizes to raise ValueError.

question: Why document the AnyIO security update in the changelog?
answer: Added a v1.14.2.0 changelog entry dated 2026-10-20 documenting the AnyIO 4.14.2 fixes for TLS hostname certificate matching and subprocess stderr deadlocks.

question: Why replace BATMAN share references and update menus dialog?
answer: Replaced BATMAN UNC path with \\192.168.0.108\FYRShare\Tools\FYRTools\WYSIWYG for menus and conditions, and added selective update modal with Update Menus, Update Conditions, and conditional Merge options

question: Why adjust Update Menus modal layout and add merge tooltip?
answer: Removed extra bottom space by using block display and auto height, and added help icon with tooltip explaining merge vs overwrite

question: Why set generic modal z-index higher and use Help title?
answer: Elevated generic modal z-index to 3000 to display on top of other open dialogs and labeled the condition merge explanation as Help

question: Why restore Conditions.json from server and preserve mediaCondition during merge?
answer: Restored Conditions.json from \\192.168.0.108 and updated merge/init logic in main.py to dynamically preserve all categories including mediaCondition and media

question: Should we set up SSO for OpenCode / AI agent usage?
answer: No. Solo developer, no entity-level compliance requirement, so SSO (OpenCode Enterprise per-seat + central config) was rejected as unnecessary overhead. Cheap alternative if it ever becomes relevant: OpenCode Console workspace with budgets and a narrow model allowlist, or LiteLLM in front with OIDC for identity/spend/audit. Noted caveat: SSO at the client layer does not restrict anything - only Enterprise central config with other providers disabled enforces a gateway.

question: Why does Manage Conditions load the adjacent conditions.json file?
answer: The editor now requests /api/conditions without master=true, so the backend serves the conditions file beside the running WYSIWYG executable instead of the network master file.

question: Why does Manage Conditions have separate Save and Update To Server actions?
answer: Added footer buttons in the requested order: Save, Update To Server, Cancel. Save writes edits to the local Conditions.json beside the running executable via /api/save-conditions; Update To Server retains the separate network-master sync action.

question: Why are the Manage Conditions Add New Item buttons above their lists?
answer: Moved each category's Add New Item button immediately below its heading and before its condition rows for easier access.

question: Why preserve media conditions when overwriting local conditions from the server?
answer: Overwrite previously copied the server JSON verbatim, which erased locally configured mediaCondition entries if the server file omitted the category or stored an empty list. The overwrite now retains the non-empty local mediaCondition list when the server has none, while still replacing the other categories from the server.

question: Why combine local and server media conditions during overwrite?
answer: The prior overwrite safeguard only copied local mediaCondition when the server category was empty, so non-empty but incomplete server data could still replace and lose locally present entries. Overwrite now unions local and server mediaCondition items, deduplicating by normalized media type plus title with server records taking precedence, while preserving unkeyed entries.

question: Why align OOP, tracks, and save with the Media Type dropdown?
answer: Grouped OOP, Tracks, and the dynamically-created save button in a 22px flex row bottom-aligned with the Media Type control, with centered contents, so their controls share the dropdown's vertical level.

question: Why should Update Menus overwrite replace local media conditions exactly like sleeve conditions?
answer: The user confirmed overwrite should discard local test edits and use the server copy as authoritative. Removed the special mediaCondition union from the overwrite path; it now writes the parsed server JSON verbatim to the local Conditions.json, matching sleeve-category overwrite behavior. The separate merge=true path remains deduplicating/combining.

question: Why do local values win duplicate keys in Update Menus merge?
answer: Merge now loads server entries first and local entries second, so it retains additions from both sources while a local entry wins when the same category, media type, and normalized title exists in both. This preserves local edits rather than silently replacing them with the server copy.

question: Why does Edit Conditions always show Add and Cancel, with Copy available for a selected entry?
answer: The Edit Conditions modal now shows Add and Cancel on initial load. Selecting an entry changes Add to Update and reveals Copy, with action order Update, Copy, Cancel. Copy immediately duplicates the selected entry's text and media type, appending '(copy)' to its title; it is not marked as a favorite by default.

question: Why should Copy in Edit Conditions stage a draft instead of saving immediately?
answer: Copy now fills the form with the selected entry's values and '(copy)' title, leaving the duplicate unsaved and editable until the user clicks Update. This prevents the list from refreshing or losing the current selection before the user confirms.

question: Is .agents/rules/tokensaver.md in conflict with AGENTS.md?
answer: No. tokensaver.md is scoped to the user's VS Code agents only - it is not meant to govern OpenCode/Claude-style sessions. Do not flag its 'absolute brevity / omit all chat text' rules as conflicting with AGENTS.md's decision-logging mandate, and do not propose merging or deleting it during instruction-file cleanup.

question: Where should persistent info about the user live, and should AI-Memory be removed?
answer: Removed AI-Memory/ (memory.md + memory.db, both git-tracked, zero references anywhere, all sections empty since 2026-03-24) - it competed with .continuity as the memory system while holding nothing. Persistent user/project info lives in .continuity/decisions.json (author: XenoHead on 18 entries), .continuity/SESSION_NOTES.md, and docs/CONVENTIONS.md (working preferences embedded as rules: pixel parity, user tests changes himself, never commit/push unasked, push only to main, accent-color contrast rules). There is no USER.md/SOUL.md and OpenCode does not read one; a dedicated profile file only helps if a loaded file (AGENTS.md or CONVENTIONS.md) points at it, since AGENTS.md is Continuity-generated and would overwrite edits.

question: Why should Cancel close Edit Conditions when no edit is active?
answer: Cancel now closes the Edit Conditions modal in its initial state. When an item is being edited or a copied item is staged as a draft, Cancel instead discards the pending form changes and returns to Add mode.

question: Where do durable facts about the user live?
answer: docs/USER.md, created 2026-10-23, with docs/CONVENTIONS.md carrying a pointer to it at the top so it is found at session start. Chose docs/ over repo root to avoid adding to the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md clutter. USER.md holds identity (handle XenoHead, solo dev), environment (Windows, workspace path, agents in use), projects, and working preferences (user tests changes himself, no commit/push unasked, UI-edit discipline, pixel parity, nomenclature). Remaining unknowns (real name, timezone, response-style preference) are listed as questions to ask, not invented. AGENTS.md cannot hold this because it is fully Continuity-generated and would overwrite edits.

question: Why place OOP, Tracks, and Save beside the Media Type dropdown?
answer: Moved the quick controls inside the Media Type control group, beside the LP/CD/CASS selector. They now share its 22px control row rather than aligning to the bottom of the taller condition lists.

question: Where do global user facts and global agent instructions live?
answer: Global, outside any repo: C:\Users\Scott\.local\share\opencode\USER.md holds durable facts about the user (identity, environment, projects, working preferences) because the user works across many projects, not just WysiWyg-Browser. C:\Users\Scott\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md holds global agent instructions and is auto-loaded by OpenCode in every project; it points at USER.md and repeats three non-negotiables (user tests changes himself, no commit/push unasked, change only what was asked). Repo docs/CONVENTIONS.md now points to the absolute global path for tools that only read the repo. Repos keep their own project-specific conventions and .continuity/decisions.json because those are genuinely per-project and Continuity resolves .continuity/ relative to the repo root.

question: Why is .continuity/decisions.json not moved to the global opencode directory?
answer: Because it is project data, not user data. Continuity resolves .continuity/ relative to each repo root, so moving decisions.json would break the continuity CLI and merge unrelated projects' decisions together. Each project (WysiWyg-Browser, WysiScan, WysiChat, Uberpaste) keeps its own decision log and session notes; only user-level facts moved to C:\Users\Scott\.local\share\opencode\USER.md.

question: What is the agent's name and where is its identity stored?
answer: The agent is named Kit (chosen by Scott 2026-10-23 from a shortlist). Identity and working style live in C:\Users\Scott\.local\share\opencode\SOUL.md, global and outside any repo, alongside USER.md (facts about Scott). Split of responsibilities: USER.md = facts about the user, SOUL.md = who the agent is and how it conducts itself, repo AGENTS.md + docs/CONVENTIONS.md = project rules, .continuity/decisions.json = project decisions. Global C:\Users\Scott\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md is auto-loaded in every project and points at both USER.md and SOUL.md.

question: Why was docs/CONVENTIONS.md deleted and restored?
answer: Agent error: a stray Remove-Item for docs/CONVENTIONS.md was included in a shell command the user never asked for, deleting the file. Recovered immediately with git checkout (tracked, committed), then re-applied the in-session edit pointing at the global USER.md that was lost in the restore. No other files affected. Rule adopted: before any destructive command, re-read the command and confirm the user asked for that specific file to be removed.

question: Why does the build copy Conditions.json beside WYSIWYG.exe?
answer: The application reads Conditions.json from the executable's directory in frozen mode, but !build.bat previously omitted it from the onedir output. The build now checks key prerequisites, runs from the script directory, stops on PyInstaller failure, and copies the current Conditions.json beside dist\\WYSIWYG\\WYSIWYG.exe so the packaged app uses the expected condition data.

question: How do we guarantee a new session knows who Kit and Scott are?
answer: Three layers. (1) C:\Users\Scott\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md is auto-injected by OpenCode in every project and now carries a summary identity block at the top (Kit; Scott/XenoHead; pointers to USER.md and SOUL.md; read-before-answering rule; three non-negotiables). (2) USER.md and SOUL.md hold the full detail and always win over the summary if they conflict. (3) Repo files hold project rules only. Rationale: USER.md and SOUL.md are NOT auto-loaded by the harness, so a session that never opens them would otherwise start blind; the inline block removes that dependency while accepting limited duplication, resolved by an explicit precedence rule.

question: Verified: does the global identity setup work from a session with no project open?
answer: Yes, verified 2026-10-23. Scott started a fresh conversation outside any project; the new session knew itself as Kit and knew him as Scott without being told, confirming that C:\Users\Scott\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md is injected even with no workspace, and that the pointer chain to USER.md (and SOUL.md) is followed rather than just the inline summary. No fallback needed: the opencode.jsonc 'instructions' array workaround is not required at this time.

question: How is THREAD.md wired into session start?
answer: THREAD.md (global handoff notes, created by a prior session) was an orphan: nothing referenced it, so a fresh session could never find it. Wired via one conditional rule in global C:\Users\Scott\.config\opencode\AGENTS.md: if THREAD.md exists and its 'Last touched:' date is within 7 days, read it at session start; if older, flag it as stale and ask before relying on it. Deliberately conditional rather than always-loaded so stale handoff notes do not pollute every session. Also moved the durable fact 'free plan, avoid per-turn overhead' out of THREAD.md into USER.md (How to work with them), since preferences belong in USER.md, and corrected THREAD.md's own header which still claimed it was never read.

question: Why exclude secrets and preserve user data in WYSIWYG builds/installers?
answer: Removed .env from PyInstaller inputs and made frozen app configuration load only from a user-provided .env beside the executable, preventing secrets from shipping in builds. Inno Setup now excludes user JSON files from the broad app copy, installs data.json/media_formats.json only when absent, preserves those and Conditions.json during uninstall, removes broad wildcard/folder deletion rules, and documents the actual onedir package layout.

question: Why does the Edit Conditions add-option media type follow the list filter?
answer: Keep the Add New Option media type aligned with the modal's selected Media Type filter so the editing controls remain consistent and new options default to the currently filtered media type.
